newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS WIN EUROPEAN SUPER CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS WIN EUROPEAN SUPER CUP.

text.p: Juventus, completing an academic task, won the European Super Cup on Wednesday when they beat Paris St Germain 3-1 in the second leg after routing the French side 6-1 in the first leg.
Italy international Alessandro Del Piero gave the European champions the lead with a well-taken goal in the 30th minute.
He made it 2-1 in the 70th, six minutes after Brazilian Rai had equalised from the penalty spot.

Substitute striker Christian Vieri, seconds after seriously testing goalkeeper Bernard Lama with a brilliant stop and volley from the edge of the area, headed in the third goal in injury time from a Del Piero cross.
Juventus's victory in the Super Cup, contested by the European Cup and Cup Winners' Cup holders, was largely academic given the Italians' 6-1 advantage from last month's first leg in Paris.
But both sides played exciting football in front of 35,000 fans in Palermo, where Juventus had obtained UEFA permission to play as attendance was expected to be low in their home city of Turin.
"This was a confirmation for us. We came here wanting to see the kind of spirit we showed in the first leg. And we saw it," Del Piero said.

"Now I've got to join the national team and we'll see what happens," added the striker, who is set to be Gianfranco Zola's back-up in Italy's key World Cup qualifier against England at Wembley next Wednesday.

Del Piero's first goal -- a short-range blast from a Moreno Torricelli pass -- came after an evenly-balanced half-hour in which PSG's Dely Valdes and Patrice Loko forced fine saves from Italy goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi.

If those saves reassured most Italians that Peruzzi is the right man to defend their goal against England, the robust goalkeeper's clumsy tackle on Valdes in the 64th minute may have changed a few minds.

Rai's equalisier from the resultant penalty appeared to ensure that the French side would at least save face after the humiliating first leg. But Juventus were evidently not going to let their devoted Palermo supporters go home without a victory.

Fans at La Favorita stadium had to wait only six minutes before erupting into cheers as Del Piero, exploiting a marred clearance by Paul Le Guen, headed in the rebound of his first shot which Lama had blocked.

"This victory was possible thanks to the fantastic crowd we found here in Palermo," Juve coach Marcello Lippi said. "They made sure we played hard, which was important because this PSG was totally different from the side we saw in the first leg.
"With this victory, we have ended a cycle which we began when we won the Italian league title in 1995. From tomorrow we must begin a new cycle."

Juventus, who won the World Club Cup in December and are two points clear at the top of Serie A, have long been more Italy's soccer team than that of Turin, where Torino have traditionally enjoyed greater support.
The club has a particularly strong following in the south which, apart from Naples, lacks any Serie A clubs.
